# Introduction
This notebook helps you set up the project after starting a new project or cloning an existing repository. It helps to setup the project for documentation rendering and software development in a virtual environment.

 Lines starting with `!` are bash commands executed from within the notebook.

Execute the cells according to your needs, using your preferred **Python version**. You may need to **restart the kernel several times** while activating the virtual environment and installing dependencies.

> **Note:** Package management in Python can be error-prone. Be prepared to resolve issues manually or fall back to terminal commands.

# Synchronize Quarto and Jupyter Notebooks
Since only `.qmd` files are typically committed to version control, you may want to sync them with `.ipynb` files first — working in `.ipynb` files is generally more convenient. The cell below synchronizes notebooks in the `meta` and `docs/tutorials` folders.

```{python}
# pyyaml is required — install it for your Python version if needed, e.g.:
# !python3.13 -m pip install pyyaml
!pip install pyyaml

from helpers import sync_jupyter_and_quarto_in_folder

sync_jupyter_and_quarto_in_folder("..//docs//tutorials")
sync_jupyter_and_quarto_in_folder(".")
```

# Create and Activate Virtual Environment
The cell below creates and activates a new virtual environment if one does not already exist. Make sure the correct Python installation is used. After creation, restart the kernel and select the new virtual environment before continuing.

```{python}
import os 
import sys

if not os.path.exists("..//.venv"):
    !python -m venv ../.venv 
    # To use a specific Python version, replace the line above with e.g.:
    # !python3.13 -m venv ../.venv
    print("Created new virtual environment.")
    print("Python path: " + sys.executable)
    print("Python version: " + sys.version)
    !..\.venv\scripts\activate  
    raise Exception("Please select the new virtual environment as the notebook kernel before continuing.")
else:
    print("Found existing virtual environment.")
    !..\.venv\scripts\activate  
```

# Install Dependencies
The cell below installs all dependencies — for the Python package under `.\src`, the meta notebooks, and the tutorials. `handle_pip_install` reads from `pyproject.toml`. Alternatively, use `requirements_venv.txt` for a legacy installation (see the second cell).

> **Note:** You may need to restart the kernel several times and resolve some errors manually. Missing packages can always be installed later with `pip install <package-name>` (if you get `ModuleNotFoundError`).

```{python}
!pip install pyyaml 

from helpers import handle_pip_install

# Based on pyproject.toml
installed_packages  = handle_pip_install(r"pip install ..\[core]")      # package under .\src
installed_packages += handle_pip_install(r"pip install ..\[tutorials]")  # tutorial dependencies
installed_packages += handle_pip_install(r"pip install ..\[meta]")       # meta notebook dependencies
```

```{python}
# Based on requirements_venv.txt (uncomment to use)
# !pip install -r ../requirements_venv.txt
```

# Conclusion
The project is now set up. Start a **new kernel with the correct virtual environment selected** for the installations to take effect, then begin developing or continue with the `main` notebook to build the documentation.

> **Note:** The tutorials may require additional setup steps documented in the `Getting Started` notebook under `docs\tutorials`.
